records.primary_outcome_quote: Several assessments of physical performance (hand grip strength, bilateral calf raise, 2-min step test, gait speed) were measured before initiating supplementation (Baseline: Visit-2) and after approximately 6 week (Visit-3) and 12 week (Visit-4) of supplementation.
records.primary_result_quote: No significant (p < 0.05) differences were observed in the carnosine versus placebo supplementation groups for any other physical performance measure.
records.sample_size_quote: 299 participants were randomized to consume either placebo or carnosine-containing capsules
records.direction_note: Benefits limited to specific subgroups (calf-raise endurance in under-40s; step-test count in males over 40) and 'the benefits appeared to be limited to males'; no effect on grip strength or the overall sample across most measures. Same NEAT trial cohort as 39919936.

identity_notes: The retrieved literature for 'l_carnosine' is dominated by a large, separate beta-alanine (carnosine's rate-limiting dietary precursor) sports-performance literature (~45 records) that was excluded as different_substance because beta-alanine, not carnosine, is the administered agent in those trials — this is the single most important applicability caveat, since beta-alanine is commonly sold and labeled as its own distinct supplement. A second cluster is Zinc-L-Carnosine / Polaprezinc (a chelate compound of zinc and L-carnosine, marketed and studied separately for H. pylori/gastritis/mucositis/reflux indications) which was kept but flagged related_form_differs throughout, since its GI-mucosal-protectant efficacy should not be read as evidence for plain L-carnosine. A third cluster used carnosine only as an undosed ingredient within multi-component combination nutraceuticals (glaucoma, facial skin, sarcopenia, OCD/depression adjuvant-to-drug trials), limiting attribution to carnosine alone. Several histidine-containing-dipeptide (HCD) systematic reviews pool carnosine, anserine, and beta-alanine data together rather than reporting carnosine-isolated effects. Genuine isolated-oral-L-carnosine human RCT evidence exists across autism, schizophrenia, OCD, MDD, Gulf War illness, diabetic nephropathy, glucose/lipid metabolism, and physical-performance/cognition domains, with results frequently mixed or null on primary/harder endpoints even when secondary measures were positive.
